name: Shanaz Hemmati
profile: Iranian-born, UT Austin-trained engineer who co-founded Austin-based ZenBusiness with Ross Buhrdorf (2015 per company); the small-business formation/AI platform has helped 700,000+ entrepreneurs and was valued at ~$1.7B after a $205M Series C. Long-time COO, she is now Co-Founder & Executive Advisor; earlier led tech at Excite.com and HomeAway.
interesting_fact: She left Iran as a child to study in the U.S.; at ZenBusiness she led a DEI strategy reaching nearly 50% female representation across staff and management, and was named to Inc.'s 2025 Female Founders list.
deep_cut_fact: She was inducted as a 2026 Distinguished Alumna of UT Austin's Electrical & Computer Engineering department; she met co-founder Ross Buhrdorf years earlier when both worked at Excite.com.
notes: Founding year given as 2015 (company) vs 2017 (Entrepreneur). She is a Capital Factory mentor in Austin; also appeared on Startergirlz podcast. Route via ZenBusiness press.

name: Ed Thompson
profile: British software engineer who co-founded Manchester-born data-integration company Matillion with CEO Matthew Scullion in 2011. He led the team that launched Matillion ETL in 2014; the cloud data pipeline company (now pushing its 'Maia' agentic data team) raised $150M Series E at a $1.5B valuation in 2021 and reached ~$2B in later rankings.
interesting_fact: Matillion is one of the few UK tech unicorns founded in Manchester; it later built a major second hub in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: Before Matillion he spent 11 years as an IBM software consultant to UK blue-chip companies; Matillion ran for three years before he and his team shipped the flagship ETL product in 2014.
notes: Common name; identity tied to Matillion CTO. Writes bylines for DBTA, DevOps.com, Solutions Review; appeared on 'Data Sharks' podcast. Route via Matillion press.

name: Philip Kaplan
current_role: Founder, DistroKid; also makes small-batch headphones (Pud's Small Batch Headphones)
profile: Philip 'Pud' Kaplan (b. 1975) is a serial internet entrepreneur: dot-com-era satirist (Fucked Company, 2000), founder of ad network AdBrite (2004), creator of TinyLetter (sold to Mailchimp 2011) and of Fandalism, which became DistroKid in 2013. DistroKid, the flat-fee music distributor he calls the biggest in the world, was valued around $1.3B after a 2021 Insight Partners investment.
interesting_fact: Since 2024 he has gone viral on Reddit building wild novelty headphones (Helmholtz resonators, wine-cork damping, a built-in CD player, a water-pump 'rain' pair) that he sells in tiny batches from pud.com.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a children's picture book about audio, 'Music Production ABCs', published by DistroKid, and is a drummer in the death-metal side project Butchers of the Final Frontier.
notes: Very online and approachable via X (@pud) and his headphone site; Syracuse iSchool '97, gave its 2014 convocation address. DistroKid valuation detail per press reports (Insight Partners 2021).

name: Wagde Zabit
profile: Israeli software engineer from Kafr Manda in the Galilee and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (2019), the agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) company valued at $1.8B in 2021. A Technion computer-science graduate, he left a long engineering career at Check Point to co-found Orca, where he remains a hands-on senior engineer.
interesting_fact: He is one of the very few Arab-Israeli co-founders of an Israeli cybersecurity unicorn; Calcalist profiled him as 'the entrepreneur from Kafr Manda who built a cybersecurity unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: At age five his father, a math teacher turned computer instructor, gave him a Commodore 64 - the first computer in Kafr Manda - and he was programming in BASIC and Logo by first and second grade.
notes: Low public profile; an engineer rather than spokesperson (CEO Gil Geron and CTO Avi Shua front the company). Recent releases also route media via Inkhouse agency. Best route: Orca press.

name: Leng Jing (冷静)
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Mengxiang Technology (梦饷科技, formerly Aikucun / 爱库存); Vice President, China Association of Trade in Services
profile: Shanghai e-commerce executive who co-founded Aikucun in 2017 with founder/chairman Wang Min; the inventory-clearance social-commerce platform rebranded as Mengxiang Group in 2020 and raised a C round that made it a unicorn. Its B2R2C model lets millions of mostly female 'shopkeepers' resell brand stock via mini-stores; she now pitches it as a 'dual SaaS' channel for China's industrial-belt brands.
interesting_fact: By 2021 Mengxiang said it had helped 2M+ shopkeepers, 95.5% of them women (many stay-at-home mothers), earn nearly RMB 5B in income; she frames the business as creating flexible jobs for women.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Aikucun she was VP and partner at the Chinese e-commerce consultancy Zhengwang Consulting (正望咨询) and VP of Tmall service partner Ruijinlin's e-commerce and Yunxiang Digital units.
notes: Hurun lists her as founder; company records name Wang Min as founder/chairman and Leng Jing as co-founder/CEO. Gave a keynote at the June 2026 Cross-Border E-commerce Development Conference (yzwb.net). No published press email found; approach via Mengxiang corporate PR.

name: Shan Dandan (单丹丹)
current_role: Chairman & CEO, For-U Truck (福佑卡车), Beijing
profile: Founder of For-U Truck (founded 2014, launched 2015), a Beijing-based digital full-truckload freight brokerage that uses AI pricing and dispatch to match shippers with truck drivers. The company raised large VC rounds to unicorn status and filed for a Nasdaq IPO in 2021 that was shelved; Shan remains chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: For-U's 'U Public Welfare' programme feeding truck drivers on the road and funding drivers' children's education was named a 2024 outstanding project of China's national 'Nuantu' driver-welfare campaign; Shan spoke as the corporate representative at the 2025 launch.
deep_cut_fact: For-U Truck's very first order came from Deppon Logistics, whose chairman Cui Weixing Shan had known for more than ten years; Deppon later said For-U had saved it 11% on costs.
notes: Chinese-language coverage only; no published press email found. Before For-U, Shan tried internet ventures (games, food O2O) that did not take off, per Chinese profiles. Approach via For-U corporate PR.

name: Spencer Rascoff
current_role: CEO, Match Group (since Feb 2025; also directly ran Tinder from July 2025); co-founder of Pacaso
profile: Serial founder (b. 1975) who co-founded Hotwire at 24 (sold to IAC for $685M), then co-founded Zillow and ran it as CEO 2010-2019 through its IPO and 15 acquisitions. Afterwards he co-founded dot.LA, co-ownership home platform Pacaso (unicorn) and AI firm Replify via family office 75 & Sunny, before being named Match Group CEO in 2025 to turn around Tinder/Hinge.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Hotwire.com in 1999 at age 24 after stints at Goldman Sachs and TPG; it sold to IAC a few years later for $685M.
deep_cut_fact: As a Visiting Executive Professor at Harvard Business School (2020) he co-created and co-taught the 'Managing Tech Ventures' course; he also co-wrote the NYT bestseller 'Zillow Talk' (2015).
notes: Highly visible public-company CEO; previously hosted the 'Office Hours' podcast and writes open letters on LinkedIn. Pacaso is the Hurun-listed source but Match Group is his day job; route via Match Group PR or 75 & Sunny.

name: Ali Javid
profile: Co-founder and CEO of Wrapbook (founded March 2018), a payroll, accounting and AP platform for film, TV and commercial productions that hit a ~$1B valuation after a $100M Series B in Nov 2021. He is now repositioning it as an AI platform that reads invoices, updates the general ledger and answers finance questions in plain English. Previously VP of Business Development at Body Labs (acquired by Amazon in 2017).
interesting_fact: The company is named after the physical binder of onboarding, payroll documents and receipts that gets assembled at the end of every production - the 'wrap book' - which Wrapbook set out to replace.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he was VP of Business Development at Body Labs, a 3D body-modelling AI startup bought by Amazon in 2017; he holds a BBA from the University of Washington and an MBA from NYU Stern.
notes: Speaker at 2026 AICP Week (commercial production industry). Co-founders: Naysawn Naji, Hesham El-Nahhas, Cameron Woodward. No published press email found.

name: Harry O'Hanley
current_role: Co-founder and executive (without portfolio), Long Wall (formerly ABL Space Systems); was CEO until Nov 2024
profile: MIT-trained engineer and ex-SpaceX Falcon 9 engineer who co-founded small-satellite launcher ABL Space Systems with Dan Piemont in 2017; ABL hit a $1.3B valuation after a $170M round in 2021, backed by T. Rowe Price, Fidelity, Venrock and Lockheed Martin. In late 2024 the company pivoted to missile-defense test vehicles and was renamed Long Wall (2025); he handed the CEO role to Piemont and stayed on as an executive.
interesting_fact: The renamed company takes its name from the Long Walls of ancient Athens; it now builds RSX, a launch vehicle for missile-defense flight testing and threat replication, plus Ironwood, a rapidly deployable ground system.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his MIT mechanical engineering degree he holds an MIT master's in Nuclear Science and Engineering; at SpaceX his roles included on-console launch operations. He is a 2003 alumnus of Shore Country Day School in Beverly, Massachusetts.
notes: Hurun lists ABL; the company is now Long Wall (missile defense / hypersonic test vehicles, Long Beach CA), CEO Dan Piemont. No published press email. Mentor at Creative Destruction Lab space stream. Shore alumni source: https://www.shoreschool.org/news-detail?pk=1412905

name: Lawrence 'Rusty' Hofmann, MD
current_role: Professor of Interventional Radiology, Stanford School of Medicine; Chief of Industry Partnerships and Medical Director of Digital Health, Stanford Medicine; co-founder of Included Health
profile: Practising interventional radiologist (10 years at Johns Hopkins, ~15 at Stanford, where he was Chief of IR for nearly two decades) who co-founded Grand Rounds with Owen Tripp in 2011-12; Grand Rounds merged with Doctor On Demand in 2021 to form Included Health, the navigation/virtual-care company valued in the billions. He remains a Stanford professor working on AI and digital health.
interesting_fact: He has published 100+ papers on minimally invasive treatment of blood clots (DVT) and cancer, holds two patents and is Global Principal Investigator for the first clinical trial testing a venous stent.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first-ever recipient of The Ohio State University School of Medicine's Early Career Achievement Award (2010), and says he has taken several devices 'from napkin stage to world-wide use'.
notes: Goes by 'Rusty'. Hurun lists him under Included Health. Spoke on BackTable podcast ep.100 about building Grand Rounds and gave 2024-25 Stanford Radiology Grand Rounds talk 'Starting a Silicon Valley Health Tech Company to Help Patients'. Academic route via Stanford likely most effective.

name: Joanna Kochaniak
current_role: Co-founder, Upside Services (Upside cash-back app); former CTO, later listed as Distinguished Engineer - current position unconfirmed
profile: Software engineer and one of six co-founders (with CEO Alex Kinnier, Thomas Vaughan, Wayne Lin, Jan Michael Rubio and Rick McPhee) of Washington, DC-based Upside (formerly GetUpside, founded 2015-16), where she served as CTO. Upside's app gives consumers cash back on gas, groceries and restaurants funded by merchants' incremental profit; it was valued at ~$2B+ in 2021-22.
interesting_fact: Upside says its users have collectively earned more than $1 billion in cash back, and its offers are embedded in the Uber and Lyft driver apps.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Aggregator profiles suggest she was a lead software engineer at Opower (as were several Upside co-founders) before Upside, but this was not verified from a primary source. MarketScreener lists no current position. Route via Upside press.

name: Sumeet Mehta
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, LEAD Group (LEAD School), Mumbai
profile: IIM Ahmedabad (PGP 1999) and PEC Chandigarh alumnus who spent 8 years running P&G businesses across Asia-Pacific and then was CEO of Zee Learn, growing it from a Rs 20 Cr preschool franchisor to a Rs 100 Cr NSE-listed education company. In 2012 he and wife Smita Deorah co-founded LEAD, a school-edtech system for affordable private schools in small-town India; it became a unicorn in 2022 ($1.1B).
interesting_fact: LEAD started in 2012 with a single school of 14 students in a village on the outskirts of Ahmedabad and grew into a network serving over a million students across thousands of partner schools.
deep_cut_fact: At Zee Learn he led the development of the iLLUME (preschool) and Litera Octave (school) pedagogies; he grew up in a small town with both parents working as teachers, which he credits for his drive to close India's small-town education gap.
notes: Co-founded with wife Smita Deorah (co-CEO). Regular Entrepreneur India columnist and ASU+GSV speaker; appeared on Chetan Bhagat's 'Deep Talk' podcast. Only published LEAD email is partner@leadschool.in (school partnerships), not a press line.

name: Daniel Michaeli
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Glia (formerly SaleMove), New York
profile: Penn graduate and ex-Accenture analyst who co-founded SaleMove in 2012, later renamed Glia; the company sells AI-driven digital customer-service and contact-center software to banks and credit unions (700+ institutions) and became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.2B valuation). He remains CEO, pushing 'banking AI' agents and interactions.
interesting_fact: Born in New York, he grew up in Guatemala from birth to 18; he tells how his grandfather, after fleeing Czechoslovakia, built a Guatemalan plastics business that began with selling plastic combs from a bicycle.
deep_cut_fact: He swears by a 'Rhythm of Business' (ROB) system - a fixed annual cadence of board meetings and planning events used as forcing functions - which he calls the single practice he would repeat as CEO of any future company.
notes: Glia has Estonian roots (strong presence in Tallinn/Tartu). Aggregators say he studied Economics, Engineering Entrepreneurship and Film at Penn and was Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2017 (unverified). Glia's recent releases used agency Words@Work for media; no glia.com press email found.

name: Matt Schulman
current_role: If the Pave founder: CEO & Founder, Pave (compensation / Total Rewards platform, San Francisco)
profile: Identity mismatch: Front (the shared-inbox SaaS valued ~$1.7B) was founded by Mathilde Collin and Laurent Perrin, and no source links a Matt Schulman to it. The best-known Matt Schulman founder is Matt Schulman of Pave, a compensation-benchmarking platform valued at ~$1.6B in 2022; he was previously a Facebook software engineer.
interesting_fact: (Pave's Schulman) calls himself a self-proclaimed 'comp nerd' and regularly publishes data-driven posts on compensation and personal finance.
notes: Hurun's 'Front' attribution appears to be an error; likely the Pave founder (unicorn, similar valuation band). Verify before outreach. Front's founders: Mathilde Collin (exec chair) and Laurent Perrin.

name: Jiang Hua (蒋华)
current_role: Executive Director & CEO, Ruqi Mobility (如祺出行 / Chenqi Technology, HKEX: 9680), Guangzhou
profile: Career GAC Group executive (joined 1997) who has led Ruqi Mobility as CEO since June 2019, when GAC and Tencent launched it as a Guangzhou ride-hailing platform. Ruqi raised a ~$153M Series A, then listed in Hong Kong in July 2024 positioning itself as a robotaxi operator, with Pony.ai as a strategic shareholder and partner.
interesting_fact: Ruqi was co-founded by carmaker GAC and Tencent and marketed its Hong Kong IPO as an autonomous-driving operations story, running robotaxi services in the Greater Bay Area.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ruqi he spent two decades inside GAC: general manager of GAC Business/Trading (广汽商贸) 2008-2018, then head of GAC's mobility project team (2018-19) that spawned Ruqi; he holds a business-management BA from Beijing Technology and Business University (1994) and a Sun Yat-sen University MBA (2003).
notes: Hurun lists him as founder; he is better described as founding CEO of a GAC/Tencent-backed venture (corporate, not founder-owned). No published IR/press email found; HK-listed so IR route via company site / HKEX filings.

name: Mark Douglas
current_role: Founder of MNTN (NYSE: MNTN); stepped down as President & CEO on Nov 2, 2026 (succeeded by Tony Weisman); employment ends Dec 3, 2026
profile: Engineer-turned-founder who started SteelHouse in 2009 with Brooke Partelow, rebranded in 2021 as MNTN, a self-serve performance connected-TV advertising platform for small and mid-sized brands, known for owning Ryan Reynolds' Maximum Effort agency. He took MNTN public in 2025; in November 2026 the board named director Tony Weisman CEO, succeeding him.
interesting_fact: MNTN bought Ryan Reynolds' creative agency Maximum Effort, and Reynolds became MNTN's chief creative officer, giving an adtech firm a Hollywood star as CCO.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at Oracle, then as VP of Technology at eHarmony built its personality-matching technology, and later was VP of Engineering at Rubicon Project (now Magnite) before founding SteelHouse.
notes: Timing-sensitive: just left the CEO role (Nov 2026 8-K); it is unclear whether he remains chairman/director. Company emails may not route to him after Dec 3, 2026. Frequent podcast guest (Speed of Culture, Disruption Now).

name: Blake Skadron
current_role: President and co-founder, iTrustCapital (Irvine, CA); formerly titled Chief Visionary Officer
profile: San Fernando Valley native and career sales leader in alternative investments who co-founded iTrustCapital with CEO Todd Southwick in 2018. The platform lets investors hold crypto and physical gold/silver in tax-advantaged IRAs; a $125M Series A in 2022 valued it above $1.3B, and in 2026 it added U.S. stocks/ETFs, crypto loans and AI quant strategies.
interesting_fact: iTrustCapital passed $16 billion in total crypto transactions by the end of 2025 and was named to Inc.'s 2026 list of fastest-growing private companies in the Pacific region.
deep_cut_fact: Named to the Los Angeles Business Journal's LA500 in 2022, which credited his move into alternative assets with a focus on client experience over short-term revenue as the idea behind iTrustCapital.
notes: Skadron and Southwick reportedly own nearly 50% of the company together (per press summaries). Appeared on 'Action and Ambition' podcast. Route via iTrustCapital media contact.
